result:
Solution 2 is most likely correct. Its answer, $s \in \{3,4,5,7\}$ with sum 19, matches my recollection of the published result on $R(K_{s,3},\mathbb{Z}_3)$, which I believe lists exceptions at $s\in\{3,4,5,7\}$. I did not re-derive the full argument, so this rests on recall plus the internal consistency of the solution.

Its method is sound in outline. A copy of $K_{s,3}$ in $K_{s+3}$ spans all vertices, so $R > s+3$ exactly when every 3-set has nonzero cross-sum. The reduction to zero-sum-triangle-free labelings is plausible, and the case table is coherent. The $n=10$ construction (a $C_5$ blown up by 2) checks out: each color class is triangle-free, there is no rainbow triangle, and the degrees are $\equiv 0 \pmod 3$, so $S(B)=e(B)\neq 0$ for every triple. The $n=9$ impossibility is asserted with a sketch rather than fully verified, so that step is the weakest part.

Solution 1 claims the exceptions are $\{3,4,5\}$. It omits $s=7$, and its construction only shows $R > s+3$ for those values without checking that no other $s$ is exceptional. Solution 3 gives no justification and its small-case values are unsupported.

CHOICE: 2
